Topics · One God, one message

Who is meant by 'each party proud of its own'?

A verse that names no one becomes a test of its reader. Who came to mind first, and why that one?

Part 1 of 4

﴿فَتَقَطَّعُوٓا۟ أَمْرَهُم بَيْنَهُمْ زُبُرًا ۖ كُلُّ حِزْبٍۭ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

But they [i.e., the people] divided their religion among them into portions [i.e., sects] - each faction, in what it has,[960] rejoicing.

Translator's notes

[960] Of beliefs, opinions, customs, etc.

Quran · Al-Mu'minun 23:53

Translation

Don’t we all have one father? Hasn’t one God created us? Why do we deal treacherously every man against his brother, profaning the covenant of our fathers?

Original · Hebrew

הֲל֨וֹא אָ֤ב אֶחָד֙ לְכֻלָּ֔נוּ הֲל֛וֹא אֵ֥ל אֶֽחָ֖ד בְּרָאָ֑נוּ מַדּ֗וּעַ נִבְגַּד֙ אִ֣ישׁ בְּאָחִ֔יו לְחַלֵּ֖ל בְּרִ֥ית אֲבֹתֵֽינוּ׃

Malachi · 2:10

World English Bible

The verse describes something and names no one. People who had one matter cut it into pieces, and each group is delighted with its own piece. No nation, no sect, no century is given. So a sentence like this works as a test of its reader. Whoever comes to mind first tells you little about the verse, and perhaps something about where you are standing as you read it.

A question for you

When you read those words, who came to mind first?

If you sayAnother religion.
ThenThat is where most of us look first. The verse gives no name to confirm it, so keep the thought open a little longer.
If you sayA group within my own faith or community.
ThenThat is close to home, and it takes honesty to say. The verse names no group, so nothing here can confirm or deny it. The next verse has a word people argue over, and we will look at it together.
If you sayMy own group.
ThenThat takes courage, and being kind to yourself will help here. The verse is no verdict on anyone. It is a mirror you chose to look into first.
If you sayNo one. People in general.
ThenThen you are reading it as it stands, with no name in it. The next part asks whether that includes the person reading.

Part 2 of 4

﴿مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُوا۟ دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُوا۟ شِيَعًا ۖ كُلُّ حِزْبٍۭ بِمَا لَدَيْهِمْ فَرِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[Or] of those who have divided their religion and become sects, every faction rejoicing in what it has.[1147]

Translator's notes

[1147] Of beliefs, opinions, customs, etc.

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:32

Translation

In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did that which was right in his own eyes.

Original · Hebrew

בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם אֵ֥ין מֶ֖לֶךְ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אִ֛ישׁ הַיָּשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינָ֖יו יַעֲשֶֽׂה׃

Judges · 21:25

World English Bible

﴿وَإِنَّ مِن شِيعَتِهِۦ لَإِبْرَٰهِيمَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And indeed, among his kind was Abraham,

Quran · As-Saffat 37:83

The same closing words return here, joined to a word that means factions: groups split from what was one. It is an ordinary Arabic word for any people who stand together, and the Quran uses it in praise of Abraham, as one of Noah's own. So the word names no community living today. And having a group is no fault. Differences of language and people are God's work. The verse speaks of splitting the religion, then delighting in one's share.

A question for you

According to the verse, what is the fault?

If you sayBelonging to a group.
ThenThen nearly everyone would be at fault, and the Quran praises Abraham with this very word. The verse points to something more exact.
If you saySplitting the religion and delighting in one's share.
ThenThat is what the verse says. Now comes a question only you can ask: is any of that in what I hold?
If you sayI have heard this word used against a particular group.
ThenMany have, and it hurts. The word means factions, and the Quran uses it in praise as well. It has its own question.

Part 3 of 4

﴿لَّيْسَ بِأَمَانِيِّكُمْ وَلَآ أَمَانِىِّ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَـٰبِ ۗ مَن يَعْمَلْ سُوٓءًا يُجْزَ بِهِۦ وَلَا يَجِدْ لَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيًّا وَلَا نَصِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

It [i.e., Paradise] is not [obtained] by your wishful thinking nor by that of the People of the Scripture. Whoever does a wrong will be recompensed for it, and he will not find besides Allāh a protector or a helper.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:123

Translation

“I, Yahweh, search the mind. I try the heart, even to give every man according to his ways, according to the fruit of his doings.”

Original · Hebrew

אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה חֹקֵ֥ר לֵ֖ב בֹּחֵ֣ן כְּלָי֑וֹת וְלָתֵ֤ת לְאִישׁ֙ כִּדְרָכָ֔יו כִּפְרִ֖י מַעֲלָלָֽיו׃

Jeremiah · 17:10

World English Bible

Here the Quran does something you might not expect: it turns the rule on its own audience. Not by your wishes, it says, and not by the wishes of the earlier scripture's people. Your wishes come first. It is speaking to those who already follow it, and belonging alone admits no one. That can sound like hard news. It is also fair. One measure is held up to everyone, so no one is asked to accept a test their own side escapes.

A question for you

Why might a book name its own followers first?

If you saySo that they cannot use it as a weapon.
ThenThen it protects other people from them, and protects them from themselves. No one can lift this verse and point it only outward.
If you sayTo keep them humble.
ThenHumility here does real work. A person who knows their group is not enough for them can listen to others.
If you sayI do not know, and it surprises me.
ThenKeep that surprise. A text that warns its own followers before anyone else is doing what a flattering text would not.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَقَالُوا۟ لَن يَدْخُلَ ٱلْجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَن كَانَ هُودًا أَوْ نَصَـٰرَىٰ ۗ تِلْكَ أَمَانِيُّهُمْ ۗ قُلْ هَاتُوا۟ بُرْهَـٰنَكُمْ إِن كُنتُمْ صَـٰدِقِينَ١١١ بَلَىٰ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ وَجْهَهُۥ لِلَّهِ وَهُوَ مُحْسِنٌ فَلَهُۥٓ أَجْرُهُۥ عِندَ رَبِّهِۦ وَلَا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ١١٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." That is [merely] their wishful thinking. Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful." Yes, [on the contrary], whoever submits his face [i.e., self] in Islām to Allāh while being a doer of good will have his reward with his Lord. And no fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:111-112

Translation

Don’t trust in lying words, saying, ‘Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, Yahweh’s temple, are these.’

Original · Hebrew

אַל־תִּבְטְח֣וּ לָכֶ֔ם אֶל־דִּבְרֵ֥י הַשֶּׁ֖קֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר הֵיכַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ הֵיכַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה הֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָ֖ה הֵֽמָּה׃

Jeremiah · 7:4

World English Bible

﴿قُلْ بِفَضْلِ ٱللَّهِ وَبِرَحْمَتِهِۦ فَبِذَٰلِكَ فَلْيَفْرَحُوا۟ هُوَ خَيْرٌ مِّمَّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "In the bounty of Allāh and in His mercy - in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."

Quran · Yunus 10:58

The feeling of being right is the same in every group. People with opposite beliefs feel it with equal warmth, so the feeling cannot be the evidence. The Quran's reply to every claim is: bring your proof. Then it names what counts: a person who gives their whole self to God and does good, whoever they are. And joy is not forbidden. 10:58 tells people to rejoice, and says in what: God's grace and mercy, which no group owns.

A question for you

Apart from its being yours, what do you have for your group?

If you sayReasons I could show to anyone.
ThenThen you have something that can be tested, and that is what the verse asks for. Bring it out and let it be weighed by the measure you use on others.
If you sayLove. They are my family and my people.
ThenLove is real, and nothing here asks you to give it up. The verse asks only that love and proof be kept apart. They do different work.
If you sayI have never needed to ask.
ThenYou are asking now, and that is a good place to be. Looking costs nothing, and what is true in what you hold will still be there afterwards.

The same in the other books

Translation

After these things Yahweh’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”

Original · Hebrew

אַחַ֣ר ׀ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה הָיָ֤ה דְבַר־יְהוָה֙ אֶל־אַבְרָ֔ם בַּֽמַּחֲזֶ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אַל־תִּירָ֣א אַבְרָ֗ם אָנֹכִי֙ מָגֵ֣ן לָ֔ךְ שְׂכָרְךָ֖ הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 15:1

For Yahweh God is a sun and a shield. Yahweh will give grace and glory. He withholds no good thing from those who walk blamelessly. Yahweh of Armies, blessed is the man who trusts in you.

כִּ֤י שֶׁ֨מֶשׁ ׀ וּמָגֵן֮ יְהוָ֪ה אֱלֹ֫הִ֥ים חֵ֣ן וְ֭כָבוֹד יִתֵּ֣ן יְהוָ֑ה לֹ֥א יִמְנַע־ט֝֗וֹב לַֽהֹלְכִ֥ים בְּתָמִֽים׃ יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֑וֹת אַֽשְׁרֵ֥י אָ֝דָ֗ם בֹּטֵ֥חַ בָּֽךְ׃

the Psalms · 84:11-12

Don’t be deceived. God is not mocked, for whatever a man sows, that he will also reap. For he who sows to his own flesh will from the flesh reap corruption. But he who sows to the Spirit will from the Spirit reap eternal life. Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season if we don’t give up.

Original · Ancient Greek

μὴ πλανᾶσθε, θεὸς οὐ μυκτηρίζεται· ὃ γὰρ ἐὰν σπείρῃ ἄνθρωπος, τοῦτο καὶ θερίσει· ὅτι ὁ σπείρων εἰς τὴν σάρκα ἑαυτοῦ ἐκ τῆς σαρκὸς θερίσει φθοράν, ὁ δὲ σπείρων εἰς τὸ πνεῦμα ἐκ τοῦ πνεύματος θερίσει ζωὴν αἰώνιον. τὸ δὲ καλὸν ποιοῦντες μὴ ἐγκακῶμεν, καιρῷ γὰρ ἰδίῳ θερίσομεν μὴ ἐκλυόμενοι.

Galatians · 6:7-9

World English Bible

And whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for men,
